Name: UNFCCC Conference of the Parties
Statutory_Basis: UNFCCC Art. 7; COP meets annually
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Remit_And_Powers: Supreme decision-making body of the UNFCCC. Reviews implementation, adopts decisions to advance climate goals. Key COPs: COP3 Kyoto (1997), COP21 Paris (2015), COP26 Glasgow (2021), COP28 Dubai (2023), COP29 Baku (2024), COP30 Belém (2025). Adopts Global Stocktake outcomes. Governs Kyoto Protocol (CMP) and Paris Agreement (CMA) as separate decision-making bodies.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Decision-maker · Rule-setter (Decisions) · Reviewer (Global Stocktake) · Advisory to Parties · No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: DESNZ leads UK delegation; FCDO supports international negotiations
UK_Links: [ORG-002] DESNZ (Dept for Energy Security and Net Zero); [POL-029] 2030 Strategic Framework for International Climate and Nature Action

Name: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change
Statutory_Basis: UNEP/WMO Resolution 1988; endorsed by UNGA Resolution 43/53 (1988)
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Remit_And_Powers: UN body for assessing the science related to climate change. Does not conduct original research but synthesises peer-reviewed literature in Assessment Reports (currently AR6, 2021–22). Three working groups: WGI (physical science), WGII (impacts, adaptation, vulnerability), WGIII (mitigation). Also produces Special Reports (1.5°C, Ocean, Land). Provides evidence base for UNFCCC negotiations including Paris Agreement and Global Stocktake.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Reviewer · Science synthesiser · Assessor · Advisory only · No regulatory or enforcement powers
UK_Representation: UK scientists contribute as authors/reviewers; Met Office co-leads WGI work; DESNZ and FCDO liaise
UK_Links: [ORG-017] Met Office; [ORG-002] DESNZ (Dept for Energy Security and Net Zero); [ORG-003] Climate Change Committee (CCC); IPCC AR6 / Cross-chapter Papers

Name: Subsidiary Body for Scientific and Technological Advice (UNFCCC)
Statutory_Basis: UNFCCC Art. 9; permanent subsidiary body
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Remit_And_Powers: Permanent subsidiary body of the UNFCCC providing scientific and technological advice to the COP. Develops methodological guidance (e.g., GHG inventories, carbon markets, land use). Reviews IPCC reports and requests special assessments. Operates alongside SBI (Subsidiary Body for Implementation). Meets twice yearly (SB sessions).
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Advisory · Methodological guidance provider · Scientific reviewer · No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: DESNZ / FCDO / UKCEH / Met Office provide expert input
UK_Links: [ORG-002] DESNZ (Dept for Energy Security and Net Zero); [ORG-017] Met Office

Name: CBD Conference of the Parties
Statutory_Basis: CBD Art. 23; COP meets every 2 years
Remit_And_Powers: Supreme decision-making body of the CBD. Adopts decisions and strategies for implementing the Convention. COP15 (Kunming/Montreal, 2022) adopted the Kunming-Montreal GBF. COP16 (Cali, 2024) established the Cali Fund (benefit-sharing from Digital Sequence Information) and a permanent Subsidiary Body on Implementation. Next COP17 planned for Armenia 2026.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Decision-maker · Rule-setter (Decisions) · Reviewer · No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: Defra leads UK delegation; JNCC provides expert advice
UK_Links: [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs); [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); UN Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) / Kunming-Montreal GBF

Name: Subsidiary Body on Scientific, Technical and Technological Advice (CBD)
Statutory_Basis: CBD Art. 25; permanent subsidiary body
Remit_And_Powers: Principal scientific advisory body to the CBD COP. Provides assessments and advice on scientific, technical and technological issues. Reviews information from IPBES. Develops monitoring frameworks and indicator frameworks (e.g., GBF monitoring framework). Meets annually or biennially alongside SBI.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Advisory · Scientific reviewer · Indicator developer · No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: JNCC and Defra scientists contribute; UK experts serve on expert groups
UK_Links: [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs)

Name: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
Statutory_Basis: UNEP Governing Council Decision 2012/1; independent intergovernmental body (not UN but UNEP provides secretariat)
Remit_And_Powers: Independent intergovernmental body established 2012, analogous to IPCC but for biodiversity. Synthesises scientific evidence on biodiversity, ecosystem services and their linkages to human well-being. Produced: Global Assessment (2019); regional assessments; thematic assessments (pollination, land degradation, invasive alien species 2023). Evidence base for GBF and national NBSAPs. 145 member governments.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Reviewer · Science synthesiser · Assessor · Advisory only · No regulatory or enforcement powers
UK_Representation: UK scientists contribute as authors; JNCC, NE and academic institutions involved; DESNZ and Defra liaise
UK_Links: [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [ORG-005] Natural England; [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs); IPBES Global Assessment

Name: UNCCD Conference of the Parties
Statutory_Basis: UNCCD Art. 22; COP meets every 2 years
Remit_And_Powers: Governing body of the UNCCD reviewing implementation of the Convention. Adopts LDN targets and strategies. COP15 (Riyadh 2022) adopted the Riyadh Declaration on drought. COP16 (Riyadh 2024). Science-Policy Interface (SPI) provides scientific advice. Operates alongside SB (Subsidiary Body for Scientific and Technological Advice) and CRIC (Implementation Review Committee).
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Decision-maker · Rule-setter (Decisions) · Reviewer · No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: Defra represents UK
UK_Links: [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs)

Name: OSPAR Commission
Statutory_Basis: OSPAR Convention Art. 10; legally binding decisions on Contracting Parties
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-013] OSPAR Convention for the Protection of the Marine Environment of the North-East Atlantic
Remit_And_Powers: Governing body of the OSPAR Convention. Composed of 15 governments and European Union. Can adopt legally binding Decisions and non-binding Recommendations. Manages Biodiversity Committee (BDC), Hazardous Substances and Eutrophication Committee (HASEC), Offshore Industry Committee (OIC), Radioactive Substances Committee (RSC) and Environmental Impacts of Human Activities Committee (EIHA). Adopted North-East Atlantic Environment Strategy (NEAES) 2030. Secretariat in London.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Regulator (within member states) · Decision-maker · Standard-setter · Legally binding decisions on Parties · MPA designator (ABNJ) · Monitoring coordinator
UK_Representation: Defra leads; JNCC provides scientific input; MMO, Cefas contribute
UK_Links: [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs); [ORG-008] Marine Management Organisation (MMO); [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [ORG-018] Centre for Environment, Fisheries and Aquaculture Science (Cefas); [LEG-022] Marine Strategy Regulations 2010 (as amended); [POL-028] UK Marine Strategy (UKMS) 2025 — Programme of Measures

Name: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea
Statutory_Basis: ICES Convention 1902 (revised 1964); non-binding advisory body
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-013] OSPAR Convention for the Protection of the Marine Environment of the North-East Atlantic
Remit_And_Powers: Intergovernmental organisation providing scientific advice on marine ecosystems and fisheries in the North Atlantic and adjacent seas. Conducts fish stock assessments used by EU, UK, Norway and others for fisheries management. Provides scientific basis for OSPAR marine environment assessments. Advises on ecosystem approach. 20 member countries. Annual WG process.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Scientific adviser · Fish stock assessor · Ecosystem assessor · Advisory only · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: Cefas, Marine Scotland Science and AFBI are major contributors; UK scientists chair several WGs
UK_Links: [ORG-018] Centre for Environment, Fisheries and Aquaculture Science (Cefas); [ORG-008] Marine Management Organisation (MMO); [LEG-022] Marine Strategy Regulations 2010 (as amended)

Name: UN Environment Programme
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Climate | Governance, Society & Data
Statutory_Basis: UNGA Resolution 2997 (1972); Nairobi Declaration 1997; UNGA Resolution 67/251 (2012) upgraded status
Remit_And_Powers: The principal UN body for the global environment. Hosts secretariats for CBD, CMS, CITES, Basel/Rotterdam/Stockholm Conventions, Ramsar, Vienna Convention/Montreal Protocol. Co-founded IPCC (with WMO). Coordinates UN-REDD Programme. Publishes State of the Global Environment reports and GEO assessments. UNEP Finance Initiative supports green finance. Based in Nairobi.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Coordination · Secretariat host · Policy adviser · No binding powers over member states
UK_Representation: UK contributes financially; Defra and FCDO liaise; UK scientists and experts contribute
UK_Links: [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs); [ORG-002] DESNZ (Dept for Energy Security and Net Zero); [POL-029] 2030 Strategic Framework for International Climate and Nature Action

Name: UN Environment Programme World Conservation Monitoring Centre
Statutory_Basis: Established 1988 as independent body; now joint unit of UNEP and WCMC (UK-registered charity)
Remit_And_Powers: Global biodiversity data and assessment centre based in Cambridge, UK. Maintains key databases: World Database on Protected Areas (WDPA), World Database of Key Biodiversity Areas (KBAs), Ocean+ data. Provides capacity building for national nature accounting. Manages ENCORE and co-developed TNFD methodology. Supports CBD monitoring framework and IPBES assessments.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Data provider · Capacity builder · Advisory · No regulatory or enforcement powers
UK_Representation: Close collaboration with JNCC, Natural England, Defra; UK-registered charity element
UK_Links: [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [ORG-005] Natural England; [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs); ENCORE / TNFD Framework

Name: UN Development Programme
Statutory_Basis: UNGA Resolution 2029 (1966)
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Remit_And_Powers: UN's lead development agency. Administers Global Environment Facility (GEF) projects. Co-founded TNFD with UNEP FI, WWF and Global Canopy. Manages Biodiversity Finance Initiative (BIOFIN). Supports countries to implement NDCs, NBSAPs and SDGs. Key channel for climate and nature finance to developing countries.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Development financer · Technical assistance provider · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: FCDO partners with UNDP on international development
UK_Links: [ORG-002] DESNZ (Dept for Energy Security and Net Zero); [POL-029] 2030 Strategic Framework for International Climate and Nature Action

Name: Global Environment Facility
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Climate | Governance, Society & Data
Statutory_Basis: Established 1991 as World Bank pilot programme; restructured as independent financial mechanism serving UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm Convention
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Remit_And_Powers: International financial mechanism and partnership of 186 countries, international institutions, NGOs and private sector. Provides grants and concessional finance to developing countries for environment-related projects. Serves as financial mechanism for UNFCCC, CBD, UNCCD, Stockholm (POPs), Minamata (mercury) and Vienna (ozone) Conventions. Has provided $22bn+ since 1991. GEF-8 (2022–26) allocates $5.33bn.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Financer · Grant maker · Concessional lender · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: UK is donor country; FCDO manages UK GEF contributions
UK_Links: [POL-029] 2030 Strategic Framework for International Climate and Nature Action; [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs)

Name: World Meteorological Organisation
Statutory_Basis: WMO Convention 1950; specialised agency of the UN
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Remit_And_Powers: UN specialised agency for meteorology, operational hydrology and related geophysical sciences. Co-founded IPCC (with UNEP). Maintains Global Climate Observing System (GCOS) — essential for tracking climate change. Coordinates Global Atmosphere Watch. Publishes annual State of Global Climate reports. IPCC Secretariat is hosted by WMO. Works with national meteorological services including Met Office.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter (meteorological) · Data coordinator · Science publisher · Advisory · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: Met Office is UK national meteorological service and contributes extensively; DESNZ liaises
UK_Links: [ORG-017] Met Office; [ORG-002] DESNZ (Dept for Energy Security and Net Zero)

Name: Global Climate Observing System
Statutory_Basis: Established 1992; co-sponsored by WMO, IOC-UNESCO, UNEP, ICSU
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Remit_And_Powers: Interagency body ensuring long-term reliable observations of Earth's climate system. Maintains Essential Climate Variables (ECVs) — 54 variables covering atmosphere, ocean, land and cryosphere. Used to monitor compliance with Paris Agreement, produce IPCC assessments and UNFCCC National Communications. Works with space agencies (ESA, NASA, EUMETSAT) and in-situ observation networks. Ocean-domain counterpart: the Global Ocean Observing System (GOOS, [INT-O-025]), which defines Essential Ocean Variables.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter (ECVs) · Observation system coordinator · Advisory · No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: Met Office, UKCEH, NERC, CEDA contribute; CEH manages UK terrestrial ECVs
UK_Links: [ORG-017] Met Office; [POL-025] UK National Climate Science Partnership (UKNCSP); [POL-027] UK Environmental Observation Framework (UKEOF)

Name: World Wide Fund for Nature (International)
Statutory_Basis: Non-governmental; Swiss foundation (1961)
Remit_And_Powers: World's largest conservation organisation. Runs the Living Planet Report (flagship publication with Living Planet Index). Active in UNFCCC and CBD COP negotiations as observer. Co-founded TNFD (with UNEP FI, UNDP, Global Canopy). Campaigns on 30×30, forests, marine protection, climate. Has 5 million+ supporters globally; offices in 100+ countries.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Campaigner · Policy advocate · Science publisher · Fundraiser · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: WWF-UK based in London; contributes to Defra consultations
UK_Links: [POL-022] 30×30 Technical Working Group; [POL-003] UK National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; [POL-012] Green Finance Strategy 2023

Name: International Union for Conservation of Nature
Statutory_Basis: Founded 1948; not a UN body but has official observer status at UNGA
Remit_And_Powers: World's largest and most diverse environmental network — union of government and civil society organisations. Produces Red List of Threatened Species (authoritative global standard for extinction risk). Manages World Database of Protected Areas. Produces Green Status of Species, Nature-based Solutions standard. Manages Peatland Code internationally. Provides expert advice to CBD, CITES, CMS, Ramsar. 160+ country members.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter (Red List, NbS) · Advisory · Data provider · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: UK member organisations include JNCC, Natural England, RSPB, Wildlife Trusts; UK government has Category B member status
UK_Links: [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [ORG-005] Natural England; [POL-031] Peatland Code; JNCC UK Biodiversity Indicators

Name: Conservation International
Statutory_Basis: Non-governmental; US non-profit (1987)
Remit_And_Powers: US-based international conservation NGO. Partners with governments on nature-based solutions, protected areas, and climate-nature finance. Science-based approach with work on biodiversity metrics and high biodiversity value areas. Contributes to IPBES and CBD processes. Key partner in 30×30 global initiative and High Ambition Coalition for Nature and People.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Campaigner · Science partner · Policy advocate · Project deliverer · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: Engages with FCDO and Defra on international nature programmes
UK_Links: [POL-029] 2030 Strategic Framework for International Climate and Nature Action; [POL-003] UK National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025

Name: Taskforce on Nature-related Financial Disclosures
Statutory_Basis: Launched June 2021; market-led, government-supported initiative; not a UN body
Remit_And_Powers: Global framework for businesses and financial institutions to assess, manage and disclose nature-related risks, impacts, dependencies and opportunities. Final recommendations published Sept 2023 (v1.0). Uses LEAP approach (Locate, Evaluate, Assess, Prepare). Mirrors TCFD structure. Implements GBF Target 15 (business and financial sector). 500+ adopter organisations representing $6.5 trillion market cap by Jan 2025. UK government encourages adoption.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter (voluntary disclosure) · Capacity builder · Advisory · No regulatory or enforcement powers
UK_Representation: UK government supporter; FCA monitors adoption; Green Finance Institute involved; UNEP-WCMC contributed to methodology
UK_Links: [POL-012] Green Finance Strategy 2023; ENCORE / TNFD Framework; [ORG-007] Office for Environmental Protection (OEP)

Name: Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures
Statutory_Basis: Established 2015 by FSB (Financial Stability Board); recommendations published 2017; disbanded 2023 with recommendations mainstreamed
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Remit_And_Powers: Developed global voluntary framework for companies to disclose climate-related financial risks and opportunities. Four pillars: Governance, Strategy, Risk Management, Metrics and Targets. Mandatory TCFD-aligned disclosure required for UK-listed companies and large private firms from April 2022. Now mainstreamed into ISSB standards (IFRS S2). Parent framework for TNFD.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter (now mainstreamed to ISSB) · No current regulatory powers (disbanded)
UK_Representation: FCA mandated UK TCFD disclosure; UK was early mover
UK_Links: [POL-012] Green Finance Strategy 2023; [ORG-002] DESNZ (Dept for Energy Security and Net Zero)

Name: GBF Monitoring Framework / GBF Indicators Portal
Statutory_Basis: CBD COP15 Decision 15/4 (2022) mandated the monitoring framework; indicators portal managed by UNEP-WCMC
Remit_And_Powers: Formal monitoring framework for the Kunming-Montreal GBF comprising headline (21), component (98) and complementary indicators. Headline indicators include Red List Index, Living Planet Index, Species Protection Index, Biodiversity Finance Index. Portal at gbf-indicators.org provides access to indicator data. Requires countries to report progress against GBF targets through updated NBSAPs and national reports.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter (monitoring) · Data coordinator · Advisory · No enforcement powers
Secretariat_Location: Montreal, Canada (CBD Secretariat) / Cambridge, UK (UNEP-WCMC portal)
UK_Representation: UK reports through NBSAP; JNCC provides data contributions
UK_Links: [POL-003] UK National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) 2025; [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); JNCC UK Biodiversity Indicators

Name: Science Based Targets Network
Statutory_Basis: Multi-stakeholder initiative led by WRI, IUCN, WWF, CI, CDP and WEF (2019); voluntary
Remit_And_Powers: Develops science-based targets for nature (SBTs for Nature) to help companies set measurable, actionable targets for their impacts and dependencies on land, freshwater, ocean, biodiversity and climate. Complements Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi) for climate. Implements GBF Target 15. Corporate target-setting piloted 2022; guidance v1.0 2023.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter (voluntary) · Capacity builder · Advisory · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: UK businesses engage; Defra and FCA monitor
UK_Links: [POL-012] Green Finance Strategy 2023; ENCORE / TNFD Framework

Name: IPBES-IPCC Joint Work Programme
Statutory_Basis: Agreed by IPBES Plenary (2021) and IPCC at 54th session (2021)
Parent_Convention: [INT-L-001] UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
Remit_And_Powers: Formal collaboration between IPBES and IPCC to address the biodiversity-climate nexus. Produced first joint IPBES-IPCC workshop report on biodiversity and climate change (2021) — landmark document showing 30–50% of terrestrial area needs to be effectively conserved or restored for climate mitigation. Influences GBF Target 2 and Paris Agreement implementation. Ongoing joint scenario analysis.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Scientific collaborator · Report producer · Advisory · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: UK scientists contribute; Met Office, UKCEH involved
UK_Links: [ORG-017] Met Office; [ORG-004] Joint Nature Conservation Committee (JNCC); [POL-025] UK National Climate Science Partnership (UKNCSP)

Name: Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission
Statutory_Basis: Established 1960 as a body within UNESCO with functional autonomy; ~150 member states
Remit_And_Powers: UN body coordinating global ocean science, services and capacity. Coordinates the Global Ocean Observing System (GOOS, [INT-O-025]), the UN Ocean Decade [INT-P-033], global tsunami warning systems, and ocean data/information exchange (IODE). Provides the scientific basis for ocean-climate monitoring and SDG 14 reporting.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Observation system coordinator · Standard-setter (ocean data/EOVs) · Capacity-building · Advisory · No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: UK member state; National Oceanography Centre and Met Office engage; UK contributes to GOOS and Decade Actions
UK_Links: [ORG-017] Met Office; National Oceanography Centre (NOC); [POL-025] UK National Climate Science Partnership (UKNCSP); [ORG-001] Defra

Name: Global Ocean Observing System
Statutory_Basis: Established 1991; co-sponsored by IOC-UNESCO, WMO, UNEP and ISC
Remit_And_Powers: International system coordinating sustained ocean observations (physical, biogeochemical, biological). Defines Essential Ocean Variables (EOVs) - the ocean counterpart to GCOS's Essential Climate Variables [INT-O-015] - including sea-surface and subsurface temperature, sea ice, sea level, ocean carbon and biology. Integrates platforms such as Argo floats, moorings, gliders and satellites; underpins ocean-temperature monitoring, operational forecasting and climate/marine assessments.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter (EOVs) · Observation system coordinator · Advisory · No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: Met Office and National Oceanography Centre contribute (operational ocean forecasting, UK Argo programme)
UK_Links: [ORG-017] Met Office; National Oceanography Centre (NOC); [POL-025] UK National Climate Science Partnership (UKNCSP); [POL-027] UK Environmental Observation Framework (UKEOF)

Name: Arctic Council
Statutory_Basis: Established 1996 (Ottawa Declaration); high-level intergovernmental forum, not treaty-based; decisions by consensus
Remit_And_Powers: Leading forum for cooperation among the eight Arctic states (Canada, Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Russia, Sweden, USA) and six Permanent Participants (Indigenous organisations) on environment, climate and sustainable development. Produces influential scientific assessments via working groups (AMAP [INT-O-027], CAFF, PAME, etc.). No regulatory powers but has catalysed binding instruments (e.g. Arctic search-and-rescue and oil-pollution agreements). Activities were largely paused after February 2022 and have since partially resumed; Chairship passed to Denmark in 2025.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Forum / consensus body · Assessment producer · Advisory · No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: UK is an Observer State (since 1998); FCDO Polar Regions Department leads; British Antarctic Survey and Met Office engage scientifically
UK_Links: [ORG-039] FCDO (Polar Regions Department); British Antarctic Survey (BAS); [ORG-017] Met Office; [POL-025] UK National Climate Science Partnership (UKNCSP)

Name: Arctic Monitoring and Assessment Programme
Statutory_Basis: Established 1991; a working group of the Arctic Council
Remit_And_Powers: Monitors and assesses Arctic pollution and climate-change impacts on ecosystems and human health, advising ministers on priority actions. Flagship outputs include the SWIPA (Snow, Water, Ice, Permafrost in the Arctic) assessments and biennial Arctic Climate Change Updates - the latest, Arctic Climate Change Update 2024: Key Trends and Impacts (published June 2025), reports Arctic warming of ~3.0 C since 1971, over three times the global mean, with record permafrost thaw and sea-ice/snow loss. Supports the UNFCCC, Stockholm and Minamata Conventions.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Assessment producer · Monitoring coordinator · Advisory · No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: UK engages via Observer-State status on the Arctic Council; Met Office (Polar Climate Group) and BAS contribute expertise
UK_Links: [ORG-017] Met Office; British Antarctic Survey (BAS); [ORG-039] FCDO (Polar Regions Department); [POL-049] Marine Climate Change Impacts Partnership (MCCIP)

Name: European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization
Policy_Sector: Biosecurity | Nature & Biodiversity | Land Use & Agriculture
Statutory_Basis: Intergovernmental organisation founded 1951; the Regional Plant Protection Organization (RPPO) for the Euro-Mediterranean region under Article IX of the IPPC
Remit_And_Powers: Coordinates plant-health protection across 52 member countries (incl. the UK). Develops regional phytosanitary standards, pest risk analyses, diagnostic protocols and the EPPO A1/A2 lists of pests recommended for regulation as quarantine pests. Maintains the EPPO Global Database. Advisory and standard-setting; no enforcement powers (implementation is by national plant protection organisations such as APHA).
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter . Pest risk analyst . Science synthesiser . Advisory only . No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: UK is a member country; APHA, Forestry Commission and Defra represent the UK and contribute to expert panels
UK_Links: [ORG-020] Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA); [ORG-001] Defra; [ORG-009] Forestry Commission (FC); Plant Biosecurity Strategy for GB [POL-034]

Name: World Organisation for Animal Health (formerly OIE)
Statutory_Basis: Intergovernmental organisation founded 1924 (as the OIE); the reference standard-setting body for animal health and zoonoses under the WTO SPS Agreement
Remit_And_Powers: Sets international standards for animal and aquatic-animal health, disease surveillance and trade (the Terrestrial and Aquatic Animal Health Codes and Manuals) across 183 member countries. Collects and publishes global animal-disease information (WAHIS). Advisory and standard-setting; no enforcement powers (implementation is by national veterinary authorities). Relevant to wildlife disease, vector-borne disease range shifts under climate change, and aquatic-animal biosecurity.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter . Disease surveillance . Science synthesiser . Advisory only . No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: UK is a member country; APHA and the UK Chief Veterinary Officer represent the UK
UK_Links: [ORG-020] Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA); [ORG-001] Defra; [LEG-042] Animal Health Act 1981; [LEG-046] Aquatic Animal Health (England and Wales) Regulations 2009

Name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
Policy_Sector: Land Use & Agriculture | Nature & Biodiversity | Biosecurity
Statutory_Basis: UN specialised agency (established 1945)
Remit_And_Powers: UN specialised agency leading international efforts on food security, agriculture, forestry and fisheries; hosts the International Plant Protection Convention (IPPC) Secretariat and the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture (ITPGRFA); co-leads the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Standard-setter - Data provider - Coordination body - No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: UK is a member state; Defra and FCDO engage; UK contributes funding and expertise.
UK_Links: [ORG-020] Animal and Plant Health Agency (APHA); [ORG-001] Defra (Dept for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs)

Name: European Commission
Statutory_Basis: Executive institution of the European Union (Treaty on European Union; Treaty on the Functioning of the EU)
Remit_And_Powers: Executive of the EU; proposes and enforces EU legislation, manages EU environmental and climate policy (DG ENV, DG CLIMA) and represents the EU internationally. Co-legislator with the European Parliament and the Council of the EU.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Decision-maker - Regulator - Standard-setter - Enforcer
UK_Representation: UK is no longer an EU member (post-Brexit); the UK Mission to the EU (FCDO) maintains relations; EU rules affect UK trade.

Name: UN General Assembly
Statutory_Basis: Principal deliberative organ of the United Nations (UN Charter, 1945)
Remit_And_Powers: Main deliberative, policy-making and representative organ of the UN; adopts the Sustainable Development Goals (2030 Agenda) and proclaims international decades (e.g. UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration; UN Decade of Ocean Science). One state, one vote.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Decision-maker - Standard-setter - No enforcement powers
UK_Representation: UK is a UN member state; FCDO leads UK representation.

Name: European Environment Agency
Policy_Sector: Nature & Biodiversity | Climate | Governance, Society & Data
Statutory_Basis: Regulation (EC) No 401/2009 (consolidating Regulation (EEC) No 1210/90)
Remit_And_Powers: EU agency providing independent information on the environment to policymakers and the public. Coordinates the European environment information and observation network (Eionet). Publishes biodiversity, climate and ecosystem indicators underpinning the EU Biodiversity Strategy 2030 and 8th Environment Action Programme monitoring. Assessment and reporting body; no regulatory powers.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Evidence-provider · Indicator custodian · Assessor · Advisory only · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: UK no longer an EEA member following EU exit; cooperation continues via Eionet on a case-by-case basis

Name: United Nations Statistics Division
Statutory_Basis: UN Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC); UN Statistical Commission
Remit_And_Powers: Part of UN DESA; serves the UN Statistical Commission. Custodian of the global SDG indicator framework and the SDG Global Database; coordinates the Inter-agency and Expert Group on SDG Indicators (IAEG-SDGs) and compiles official statistics across member states. Methodological and data-coordination body; no regulatory powers.
Regulatory_Powers_Keywords: Indicator custodian · Data coordinator · Standard-setter (statistical) · No regulatory powers
UK_Representation: Office for National Statistics (ONS) contributes UK official statistics and SDG reporting

Name: Biodiversity Indicators Partnership
Statutory_Basis: Global partnership convened under the CBD; coordinated by UNEP-WCMC
Remit_And_Powers: Global partnership of organisations generating biodiversity indicators to track progress towards the Kunming-Montreal GBF and the SDGs. Coordinated by UNEP-WCMC. Maintains the BIP indicator catalogue used in GBF monitoring. Indicator development and coordination; no regulatory powers.
